title: Find out whether the layer menu promises a Duplicate key that deselects instead
goal: The right-click menu on a layer prints Command D beside Duplicate, but Command D is Deselect in the menu bar, so a person who learns the key from the menu may get the wrong thing. Check what pressing it really does and make the printed key and the real key agree.
notes: Not reproduced, only read: LayerCommandMenu.swift appends .command("Duplicate", .command("d")); EditorCommands.swift binds Deselect to keyboardShortcut("d", modifiers: .command) with a comment that Duplicate Layer has no key and Cmd-J duplicates when nothing is marqueed. The timeline clip menu (EditorState+TimelineMenus.swift) prints Cmd-J for Duplicate for this reason. Found 2026-09-23 by the right-click task.
acceptance: Pressing the key printed beside Duplicate in the layer right-click menu duplicates the layer
A walk reads the row and presses its key

log.note: digest 2026-09-24: Command D is also in play for one-key-puts-the-usual-transition-on-the-cut-at (Premiere's default transition key). Command D is Deselect in Photoshop, and the user wants Photoshop keys by default, so settle this first and hand the transition task a key that collides with nothing.

triage 2026-09-25: one-key-puts-the-usual-transition-on-the-cut-at shipped Command T for the transition and left Command D as Deselect, so the transition half of this is settled. What is left is only the layer menu printing Command D beside Duplicate.
